$comment: Dogfood projection map — example shape for `designguard` cross-checking workflows. Each entry binds one tool rule to an external judgement source (a legacy test gate, a lint script, a manual checklist) so counts can be reconciled before the legacy gate is retired. Anchors pointing at private repositories stay private; this file documents the schema and a minimal seed for the rules implemented in v0.1.

externalGate.judgement: Multi-component Margin/Padding literal with any component not in the spacing ladder [0,2,4,8,12,16,24,32]. Scan forms: attribute, property element, Setter Value. Comments stripped before scanning.
externalGate.sourceAnchor: file+line of the legacy assertion (fill in per repository)

entries.projection: Count hits with the tool rule after projecting the legacy scan surface onto the tool config scope; the projected count must equal the legacy count. Generalization deltas (e.g. extra scan forms the legacy regex missed) go to a delta list with individual dispositions.

externalGate.judgement: TextBlock with TextWrapping="Wrap" missing LineHeight or LineStackingStrategy. WrapWithOverflow intentionally out of scope.
externalGate.sourceAnchor: file+line of the legacy assertion (fill in per repository)

deltaDisposition.$comment: Every projection-vs-legacy delta gets exactly one of: fixed (tool narrowed), exempted (registered in designguard.json), or issue-tracked (with link). Clearing to zero is NOT the acceptance criterion; the dispositions ledger is.
